name: Futunan / futunien, fakafutuna
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Rensch, Karl H. (ed.). 1986. Tikisionalio fakafutuna-fakafalani / Dictionnaire futunien-français. Pacific Linguistics C-90. Canberra: Australian National University. x + 338 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-C90 (2015 open edition, CC BY-SA 4.0).
catalog_locator: p. ix (roman-numbered front matter, section 'L'orthographe et la prononciation', sub-heading 'L'ACCENTUATION')
catalog_quote: Le futunien a des voyelles longues et brèves. La longueur de la voyelle est distinctive et permet de différencier des mots comme mālo "vainqueur" et malō "sec", paki "palette de danse", pāki "imprimé". ... L'ACCENTUATION. Dans les mots de deux ou trois syllabes l'accent tombe sur l'avant-dernière syllabe. Dans les mots de quatre syllabes ou plus un deuxième accent est placé sur la quatrième syllabe avant la fin. En plus toutes les voyelles longues d'un mot sont accentuées: mata "oeil" ['mata], matagi "vent" [ma'taŋi], matikuku "griffes" ['mati'kuku], mataki "veiller", ['ma:'taki], malō "sec" ['ma'lo:].
world_status: statement found in an open source

Dans les mots de quatre syllabes ou plus un deuxième accent est placé sur la quatrième syllabe avant la fin. new_statements.translation: In words of two or three syllables the accent falls on the penultimate syllable. In words of four syllables or more a second accent is placed on the fourth syllable from the end. In addition, all long vowels of a word are accented: mata 'eye' ['mata], matagi 'wind' [ma'taŋi], matikuku 'claws' ['mati'kuku], mataki 'keep watch' ['ma:'taki], malō 'dry' ['ma'lo:].
new_statements.citation: Rensch, Karl H. (ed.). 1986. Tikisionalio fakafutuna-fakafalani / Dictionnaire futunien-français. Pacific Linguistics C-90. Canberra: Australian National University, p. ix (introduction, section 'L'ACCENTUATION'). DOI 10.15144/PL-C90.
new_statements.locator: p. ix (roman-numbered introduction; PDF page 7 of the Commons/PL file), section heading 'L'ACCENTUATION'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (338 pp., PL C-90; cover page reads "Online edition licensed 2015 CC BY-SA 4.0, with permission of PL", DOI 10.15144/PL-C90). Re-rendered PDF page 7 myself (60 dpi) and compared with the held : the page is roman-numbered ix and ends with the heading "L'ACCENTUATION" followed by exactly the quoted passage: "Dans les mots de deux ou trois syllabes l'accent tombe sur l'avant-dernière syllabe. Dans les mots de quatre syllabes ou plus un deuxième accent est placé sur la quatrième syllabe avant la fin. En plus toutes les voyelles longues d'un mot sont accentuées: mata "oeil" ['mata], matagi "vent" [ma'taŋi], matikuku "griffes" ['mati'kuku], mataki "veiller", ['ma:'taki], malō "sec" ['ma'lo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default primary stress on the penultimate syllable of the word; a secondary (rhythmic) stress two syllables further left (4th from the end) in words of four or more syllables; every long vowel is stressed regardless of position (e.g. word-final long vowel in malō, initial long vowel in mataki), so vowel length (weight) overrides/adds to the penultimate default. Equivalent to the usual Polynesian 'penultimate mora' pattern, though Rensch states it in syllables plus a long-vowel clause. He does not distinguish primary from secondary stress in his transcriptions (both marked with ').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Stated explicitly: in words of four or more syllables a second accent falls on the fourth syllable from the end (matikuku ['mati'kuku]); long vowels also carry an accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated beyond the long-vowel clause; no mention of compounds, particles, loanwords or phrase-level accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms in a dictionary introduction on orthography and pronunciation); the statement is a short editor's note, not a phonological analysis, and the standard orthography does not mark stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Rensch 1986 describes East Futunan (fakafutuna) of Futuna island, Wallis and Futuna (east2447, ISO fud), the same variety as Grézel 1878 and Moyse-Faurie; not to be confused with West Futuna-Aniwa (futu1245, Vanuatu). No dialect is specified.
